prompt: A public library index page of the Lexkite website (free, playful English-learning app for IELTS/TOEIC learners). Same site header as the Lexkite home page: kite logo + 'Lexkite', a few nav links, a candy-orange 'Start free' tactile button; friendly footer. The page shows 80 IELTS Writing Task 2 sample essays. Open with a spotlight hero rather than a plain title: a big friendly headline, one short line, three glanceable stat badges (essays, question types, band 8) each a chunky icon with a big number, and the teacher-slot standing on the hero floor. Right below, a bento mosaic of six big tappable tiles, one per question type (Agree/Disagree, Discussion, Problem–Solution, Advantages–Disadvantages, Positive/Negative, Two-part question): every tile is its own colour with its own large glossy illustrated badge, the type name and a count; one tile is larger than the others. Then a slim search field with a row of filter pills that clearly continues sideways: the pill at the edge is never chopped mid-word, a soft fade and a small round chevron show there is more. Then one group of essays: a big featured card first, spanning wider, then smaller cards. Each essay card is scanned by eye: a coloured illustrated topic badge, a short 2–4 word topic headline such as 'Free university education' in large type, one quiet line of the question below, and a small band ring with a little row of icon-and-number marks for length, phrases and reading time. No repeated type label on the cards. Not a uniform grid of text boxes. Feel: playful and warm, candy-like tactile surfaces with a soft ledge, glossy illustrated badges, rounded chunky cards, lots of breathing room. You understand the page by glancing, not by reading: almost no text, short labels only, every card recognisable by its picture and colour from across the room. Use the Lexkite Kit design system, Bright Day light theme. Every label stays easy to read (at least 4.5:1), every tap target comfortable for a thumb, labels can grow 40% longer and wrap without breaking. Draw only the page itself: no device frame, no browser chrome, no photos, no drawn people: leave one empty rounded 'teacher-slot' where a teacher character will stand on the hero floor.
